title: Normalize usage buckets and stable export signatures for mid-cycle adjustments
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary: Multiple customers observed invoice line mismatches when late quota adjustments (rate-limit refunds, burst credits) are applied mid-billing-cycle. Root causes identified: 1) Export window bucketing is not consistently aligned to a canonical boundary (UTC hour vs service-local intervals), producing borderline usage attribution when adjustments span boundaries; 2) Export job signatures are non-deterministic (timestamped filenames + non-stable ordering), leading to NetSuite import duplicates and Stripe line merging mismatches; 3) Reconciliation job is not fully idempotent for partial-window backfills.

Goal: Implement deterministic bucket normalization, produce stable export signatures, and make the reconciler idempotent and capable of safe backfill so invoices remain accurate even when late credits or rate-limit refunds are applied. This reduces duplicate export noise, prevents over/undercharging, and simplifies downstream NetSuite/Stripe reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Exported usage files are deterministically partitioned to canonical UTC boundaries and documented in export spec
Each export file has a stable signature/hash derived from (customer_id, canonical_interval_start, export_version) and is immutable once generated
Reconciler will skip already-applied export signatures to avoid double-applies; re-run of same signature is safe and no-op
Backfill job can import a late adjustment window without causing duplicate Stripe invoice lines or NetSuite sync conflicts
End-to-end integration test (staging) shows zero duplicate line items for a synthetic mid-cycle rate-limit refund scenario
Metrics: duplicate-export alerts drop to zero for the impacted cohort and Stripe reconciliation failure rate reduces by >=95% in staging
comments: 2025-01-16 - Maya T: Initial triage after ops alert. Correlated 4 customer incidents to same export window skew pattern. Filed ENG-91234 to scope deterministic export work.

2025-01-21 - Rohit K: Spike completed. Verified bucket misalignment occurs when adjustments cross DST boundary in customer timezone; decided to canonicalize to UTC hour windows to avoid timezone/DST complexity.

2025-01-24 - Rohit K: Design review with payments and integrations. Agreed on export signature format: sha256(customer_id + '|' + interval_start_iso + '|' + export_version). Added export_version to allow future format changes.
2025-01-28 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/billing-reconciler/pull/512 - implements bucket normalization and signature generation. Added unit tests for boundary conditions.

2025-01-30 - QA: Found race where two parallel exporter workers could emit same signature with different file ordering causing NetSuite import comparator mismatch. Introduced leader election per-canonical-interval to ensure single file production.

2025-02-01 - Rohit K: Reconciler idempotency added: reconcile.accept(signature) is idempotent and stores applied_signature in export_audit table. Backfill job checks audit table before attempting apply.

2025-02-02 - Maya T: Integration run in staging with synthetic rate-limit refund passed. Observability dashboards updated: billing.export.signature_count, billing.export.duplicates, billing.reconcile.failures. Moving to In Progress -> awaiting final review and runbook updates.
Action items: finish runbook, coordinate with Finance for one-time invoice corrections if required, schedule gradual rollout to production in billing-2025.02 release window.
migration_steps: 1) Deploy exporter changes to staging; run synthetic mid-cycle adjustment test suite
2) Run backfill tool in dry-run mode against staging NetSuite export simulator and verify no duplicate detections
3) Deploy export code to one region behind a feature flag; enable leader-election and signature recording
4) Monitor billing.export.duplicates and reconcile.failures for 48 hours; if stable, proceed to full rollout
5) Run one-time correction job for affected customers if Finance approves; record corrections in audit log
rollback_plan: If exporter rollout shows increased duplicate exports or reconciliation errors, flip the feature flag to the previous export implementation and roll back exporter deployment
If rollback is required after partial application of backfill, use export_audit table to identify applied signatures and run compensating transactions to reverse partial Stripe/NetSuite applies
Notify Finance + SRE and open incident with priority P0 for immediate mitigation
